The governing documents specify materially different coating regimes (hot-dip galvanising versus an epoxy/coastal treatment). Documented, but not priceable while the governing regime is unresolved. This is the FULL-001 case.
NEG-001. The inclusions list prints 'NO IRRIGATION'. The engine evidenced irrigation from that document at 0.32 confidence, reading a prohibition as a specification. It must never be evidenced.

NEG-002, the half the engine got right: 'No cornice - square set finished ceilings' SELECTS square-set. A negation is not only a deletion. No priceability claim is labelled here; the audit does not adjudicate it.

conflicts.summary: Different client/project names across title blocks
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: partly_correct. Documents do use different labels (METE FAMILY, Paul Mete/structural client naming, address-based titles, City of Port Phillip material), but all clearly relate to 108 Dow Street. It is a document-control issue, not a technical scope conflict.

Audit verdict: confirmed. Endorsed planning material is internally inconsistent: Unit 2 described as 700 L in one line while STORM tables/management notes say 800 L. Working drawings also state 800 L each. Set one governing tank requirement per dwelling.

conflicts.summary: Energy rating target conflicts (6 star vs 7 star)
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: confirmed. Inclusions list says "7 star energy rating" but also "Only a 6 star required here"; later it says 7 star. Supplied NatHERS results are 7.0 star Unit 1 and 7.2 star Unit 2. Delete the 6-star wording and state a 7-star minimum per dwelling.

conflicts.summary: 2 kW per unit vs 4.0 kW BESS solar profile
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: incorrect. 2 kW per dwelling equals 4 kW across two dwellings, so the figures are consistent. The real later-design issue is that WD Issue 6 shows 2.5 kW roof-mounted PV per dwelling. Do not flag per-unit vs total as a conflict; compare basis instead.

conflicts.summary: Party/boundary firewall has two alternative systems
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: confirmed. Architectural/inclusions material allows alternative masonry/Dincel-type 60/60/60 boundary wall solutions. These are materially different in cost, structure and interfaces. Select the governing wall system before tender, or price a base plus alternate.

Audit verdict: confirmed. Electrical drawings include provisions/connections while inclusions put CCTV, alarm, security entry, LAN and most home automation with the owner; cafe awnings, garage doors and two stair windows remain builder scope. The prewire/interface split is unclear.

conflicts.summary: Solar and landscaping shown but excluded/owner scope
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: partly_correct. Inclusions make the main responsibility fairly clear: landscaping by Paul; solar panels/inverter coordinated by owner and installed by a chosen installer. The remaining risk is builder interfaces (rough-ins, supports, penetrations, making-good), not the primary allocation.

conflicts.summary: Footing design relies on drainage/de-watering by others
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: confirmed. The structural footing detail states effective drainage/de-watering is by others and is part of the footing design assumption. The responsible designer/installer is not clearly named in the tender allocation; assign design, install, discharge, maintenance and warranty.

conflicts.summary: Balustrades noted "BY OTHERS including all fixings"
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: unsupported. Balustrade support/top-plate details are visible in the structural set, but the quoted "BY OTHERS including all fixings" wording could not be verified in the supplied structural pages. The finding overstates the evidence; remove or reword it.

conflicts.summary: EV charging shown on electrical plan but BESS says not provided
conflicts.basis: Audit verdict: partly_correct. WD Issue 6 shows two three-phase EV charging points while the earlier BESS assessment records EV infrastructure as "No". This is a document-stage mismatch, not automatically a tender contradiction; confirm which document governs.

conflicts.summary: Geotechnical report allows 100 kPa bearing while the structural design assumes 120 kPa.
conflicts.basis: CRITICAL material finding. A real engineering contradiction between two supplied consultant documents, and the canonical case for what a true conflict looks like.

conflicts.summary: Working drawings are labelled PRELIMINARY, NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION while being issued as the tender basis.
conflicts.basis: CRITICAL material finding. Document status must be read from the stamp; issuing a preliminary set as the tender basis is a document-status failure, not a scope gap.

regressions.title: An explicit negation suppresses the item
regressions.rationale: The inclusions list prints 'NO IRRIGATION'. The engine evidenced irrigation from it — reading a prohibition as a specification.

regressions.title: A negation that selects its alternative
regressions.rationale: 'No cornice - square set finished ceilings' both suppresses cornice AND selects square-set. A negation is not only a deletion.

regressions.title: Conditional items need an activation signal
regressions.rationale: Residential lift, fireplace, sewer pump, sprinklers and outdoor kitchen were gapped from possibility on a pack that shows none of them.

regressions.title: A real engineering contradiction is detected
regressions.rationale: 100 kPa allowable bearing in the geotechnical report against 120 kPa assumed in the structural design. Two supplied documents disagreeing on a number that moves the footing design.

regressions.title: Per-unit and project totals reconcile rather than conflict
regressions.rationale: 2 kW per dwelling and 4 kW project total are the same fact stated two ways.

regressions.title: A quotation must exist in the source it cites
regressions.rationale: The engine quoted 'BY OTHERS including all fixings' for balustrades; the audit could not find that wording in the cited structural source. The Wallace deck is the same failure in a different costume.

regressions.title: Conflicting governing regimes block a priceable claim
regressions.rationale: Protective coating was graded FULL while hot-dip galvanising and an epoxy/coastal treatment both governed. Documentation depth is not priceability.

regressions.title: Preliminaries are contractor obligations on a rich pack too
regressions.rationale: The same eight preliminaries lines were presented as design gaps here as on Wallace, despite ten documents being supplied. Pack richness never makes scaffolding a drawing.

regressions.title: Evidence present in a supplied document is not a gap
regressions.rationale: Ten of the 51 gaps were already evidenced somewhere in the pack — raked ceiling framing called up in WD Issue 6, tree protection zones on the drawings, garden edging in the landscape notes. On a ten-document pack this is a retrieval failure, not a judgement one.

regressions.title: Document status is read from the stamp
regressions.rationale: The working drawings are labelled PRELIMINARY, NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION while serving as the tender basis. The engine did not surface it.

notes: The rich pole of the corpus: ten documents across seven disciplines. Labels the 51 gap rows the audit reclassified, all 10 conflicts it validated, and 2 material findings the engine missed entirely. Deliberately silent on the 179 evidenced rows the audit did not individually adjudicate — the scorer only scores labelled lines, so a partial package gives honest numbers on the settled part rather than invented numbers on the whole. Paired with 57-wallace-street, which is the same engine on one document.
